html:
The Quran is the holy book of Islam, which Muslims believe God revealed to the prophet Muhammad in Arabic over about 22 years, from 610 to his death in 632. Its name means "the recitation". It has 114 chapters, called suras, made up of verses.

For Muslims it is the direct word of God, not a book written by Muhammad. It speaks of the oneness of God, the day of judgement, care for the poor, and the prophets who came before, among them Abraham, Moses and Jesus. It also gives rules for prayer, fasting, marriage, inheritance and trade.

It was first passed on mainly by memory and recitation. Followers also wrote verses on parchment, bone and palm leaves. After Muhammad died, the verses were gathered into one book. Under the third caliph, Uthman, around 650, a standard text was fixed and copies were sent to the main cities of the caliphate.

Its influence reaches far beyond religion:

  • It fixed Classical Arabic. Scholars developed Arabic grammar to understand it, and it became the model for all later Arabic writing.
  • It spread the Arabic alphabet to Persian, Turkish, Urdu, Malay and many other languages.
  • Writing out its words became one of the most honoured arts of the Islamic world, Islamic calligraphy.

Millions of Muslims learn it by heart, and it is recited in Arabic in daily prayer around the world. Alongside it, the sayings and deeds of Muhammad, the hadith, guide Islamic law and practice.
